cases.description: The Appendix A bound package: every check passes.
S2 without the Tier 2 step-up still authorizes PRESENT.
S5 absent: accepted; the risk framework applies (§3.3).
S3 absent: accepted (optional signal).
S5 as a single certified provider's submission.
signals_present omits S3, which the package carries.
package_id carries fewer than 128 bits.
afsp_version is not 0.1.
The package bound to Sunrise is presented to Pacific Savings.
The unbound reverse-inquiry package carries no institution nonce.
Presented after the nonce expired (1800 s after assembly, plus 30 s skew).
A signal member changed after the platform signed.
Signed by a key that is not a published platform key.
receiving_institution_id names Pacific; the nonce still binds Sunrise's key.
validity_window exceeds 3600 s.
validity_window starts 600 s in the future.
Two-step case: the same package is presented twice to the same verifier. The first presentation is ACCEPTED; the second is a replay.
S1 is absent (mandatory, §3.3).
The registry record shows the agent SUSPENDED.
S1 is signed by a key that is not an agent registry key.
The running build hash is not a certified build.
S2 is absent (mandatory, §3.3).
The Tier 2 token is signed by a key other than its certified tier key.
The consumer authorized a different agent than S1 identifies.
The Tier 1 authorization token is valid for more than 3600 s.
The Tier 2 token is bound to Pacific Savings.
The tier key certificate is not signed by the issuing institution.
INITIATE with only the Tier 1 discovery authorization.
The Servicing Intent Package differs from the one the step-up signed.
The requested product category (CHECKING) is outside the consumer's scope.
EXECUTE requested before PROCEED_TO_KYC.
The Tier 1 key signs an INITIATE authorization; its EKU does not permit INITIATE.
S4 is absent (mandatory, §3.3).
S4 signals carry a raw data member (account_balance_usd); §8.1 permits derived signals only.
Differential privacy epsilon 4.0 exceeds the institution's maximum (1.0).
S4 is signed by a key that is not the certified S4 provider's.
The S5 composite no longer matches its signature: logged, package accepted.
S3 attests a different enrolled consumer: treated as absent, package accepted.
